issues.title: Annotation entries admit neither description nor concepts;  rames entries are indistinguishable
issues.author: clemensv
issues.body:
Annotation-internal objects — the repeated entries inside `tensorReferenceFrames`, `vectorReferenceFrames`, `frameTransforms`, `colorSpaces`, `audioChannels`, `spectralBands`, and the component entries inside them — admit neither a `description` nor a `concepts` member. Every one of them is `"additionalProperties": false`, so an author cannot add either. Nothing in the schema can say what an individual entry is for.

The draft is aware of the problem and delegates it to the referenced definition. From the Vertical and Compound Systems section:

> The axis direction comes from the referenced definition and not from the annotation, so whether the axis is positive up or positive down is a fact about the identified system. Where `kind` is `type`, the `description` of the meta-type or of its elements states it.

That works when the entries reference different definitions. It fails when they reference the same one, because one shared description cannot say different things about different positions.

## The acute case: `frames`

`FrameReference` carries `reference`, `kind`, and an optional `variance`, and nothing else. It binds no members. Its whole meaning is its position in the array. Consider a piezoelectric strain tensor over one set of crystal axes:

```json
"tensorReferenceFrames": [
  {
    "frames": [
      { "reference": { "$ref": "#/definitions/CrystalAxes" }, "kind": "type" },
      { "reference": { "$ref": "#/definitions/CrystalAxes" }, "kind": "type" },
      { "reference": { "$ref": "#/definitions/CrystalAxes" }, "kind": "type" }
    ],
    "components": "d"
  }
]
```

Three byte-identical entries. Index 0 is the axis of the applied field; indices 1 and 2 are the axes of the strain it produces. Neither the annotation nor a description on `CrystalAxes` can carry that distinction, and no consumer or documentation generator can recover it.

This is not an edge case. The draft names the repeated-frame case as typical:

> One frame MAY be named by more than one entry, and is so named for a stress, a strain, or a seismic moment tensor.

So the annotation cannot label index positions for exactly the tensors it cites as the common ones. `FrameReference` is the worst affected because it is the only entry type that binds nothing — `VectorReferenceFrame`, `AudioChannel`, and `SpectralBand` at least name their members through `components`, `channels`, and `bands`, so a reader has something to go on.

## `concepts` on entries

`concepts` is currently reachable only through `ConceptsAddIn`, which attaches to a type definition and to property, collection item, map value, and choice member schemas. An annotation entry is none of those.

An entry is often exactly the thing worth pointing at a published term. The applied-field index of a piezoelectric tensor, a spectral band set, an audio channel group, a color space entry — each denotes something a vocabulary already names, and the entry is where that identity belongs. Today it has nowhere to go. The same argument applies to the component entries of `tensorComponents` and to `codedValues`, so this is probably worth doing uniformly rather than only where it was first noticed.

Note that `concepts` and `description` are not substitutes for each other here. One is for a machine, the other for a person, and the entries want both.

## Proposal

1. Permit an optional `description` on every annotation-internal object, most importantly on `FrameReference`.
2. Permit an optional `concepts` on the same objects, with the same shape and semantics `ConceptsAddIn` already defines.

Both are additive and neither changes the meaning of an existing schema. Factoring them into a small abstract base that the entry types extend would keep the meta-schema from repeating itself, and would make it obvious that the rule is uniform.

The alternative for point 1 — leaving the descriptive burden on the referenced definition — should be stated explicitly in the draft if it is kept, together with an acknowledgement that it does not reach the repeated-frame case.

issues.title: Allow reference string syntax to depend on kind
issues.author: clemensv
issues.body:
## Problem

The `concepts.reference` member currently requires an absolute URI. This prevents bindings to definition models whose canonical identifiers use another string syntax.

OPC UA is one example. An ExpandedNodeId with a namespace URI is canonically written as:

```text
nsu=http://opcfoundation.org/UA/;i=46
```

Wrapping that value in an invented URI scheme would replace the authoritative identifier with a private encoding. Requiring an absolute URI therefore either excludes the model or encourages non-standard identifiers.

## Proposal

Make `reference` a string whose lexical space and interpretation depend on `kind`.

- For the kinds defined by this specification (`rdfs-class`, `rdf-property`, `owl-class`, `owl-object-property`, `owl-datatype-property`, `skos-concept`, and `dcterms-property`), retain the absolute-URI requirement.
- A specification defining another `kind` may define a different string syntax and its validation rules.
- A processor that recognizes a `kind` validates `reference` according to that kind.
- A processor that does not recognize the `kind` preserves both values and reports resolution or compatibility checks as indeterminate. It must not reject the annotation solely because `reference` is not an absolute URI.
- `kind` classifies the identifier model and determines its lexical rules; equality remains equality under that model rather than generic string or URI equivalence.

Example:

```json
{
  "concepts": [
    {
      "reference": "nsu=http://opcfoundation.org/UA/;i=46",
      "kind": "opcua-reference-type-nsu"
    }
  ]
}
```

Here, `opcua-reference-type-nsu` states both the identified OPC UA node class and the ExpandedNodeId syntax used by `reference`.

## Meta-schema impact

The meta-schema should accept a string for `reference`. Rules coupling a recognized `kind` to its permitted `reference` syntax can remain semantic conformance checks when the meta-schema cannot express them directly.

## Acceptance criteria

- The specification no longer imposes an unconditional absolute-URI constraint on every `concepts.reference`.
- Every built-in `concepts.kind` still requires an absolute URI.
- Extension kinds can normatively define another reference string syntax.
- Processing and conformance sections define behavior for recognized and unrecognized kinds.
- The meta-schema accepts non-URI reference strings without weakening validation for built-in kinds.

issues.title: Allow description and descriptions on concept entries
issues.author: clemensv
issues.body:
## Problem

Each object in a `concepts` array currently permits only `reference` and `kind`. This leaves no place for a human-readable explanation of the referenced term alongside the binding.

That is inconvenient when the canonical identifier is compact or opaque, when a reference is not dereferenceable, or when a schema is reviewed offline. OPC UA NodeIds illustrate the problem:

```json
{
  "reference": "i=78",
  "kind": "opcua-modelling-rule"
}
```

A reader cannot tell from this object alone that `i=78` identifies the `Mandatory` ModellingRule. Putting that information in the annotated schema node's `description` does not scale when the node has several complementary concept entries, because the text cannot be associated unambiguously with one entry.

Concept entries are not themselves schema elements. The `descriptions` keyword from JSON Structure Alternate Names and Descriptions therefore does not automatically apply inside them, even when that extension is enabled.

## Proposal

Permit an OPTIONAL `description` string and an OPTIONAL `descriptions` map on each `concepts` entry:

```json
{
  "reference": "i=78",
  "kind": "opcua-modelling-rule",
  "description": "Mandatory ModellingRule",
  "descriptions": {
    "lang:en": "The referenced declaration must exist on every instance.",
    "lang:de": "Die referenzierte Deklaration muss in jeder Instanz vorhanden sein."
  }
}
```

`descriptions` has the shape and semantics defined by JSON Structure Alternate Names and Descriptions, Section 3.3:

- Its value is a map from purpose indicators to description strings.
- Keys beginning with `lang:` carry localized descriptions and use BCP 47 language tags.
- Other purpose keys remain available under the rules of that extension.

Both forms are informational:

- `kind` and `reference` remain the complete authoritative identity of the concept.
- Processors MUST NOT use `description` or `descriptions` for resolution, equality, compatibility, inference, or repair of an unresolved reference.
- Missing or contradictory descriptive text does not change the identified concept.
- Processors SHOULD preserve both forms.
- Schema authors SHOULD obtain descriptive text from the referenced authority where practical.

This follows the drafts' existing rule that descriptions inform readers but do not establish machine semantics.

## Specification relationship

The Semantic Annotations specification should normatively reference JSON Structure Alternate Names and Descriptions for the `descriptions` value shape and processing rules. It should not reproduce or fork that format.

The specification should state whether use of `descriptions` in a concept entry requires the `JSONStructureAlternateNames` feature. Prefer requiring that feature so the same keyword has one activation and processing model throughout a schema.

## Alternatives considered

A description on the annotated schema node describes that node as a whole. It cannot explain several concept entries independently.

Requiring every reference to resolve excludes legitimate identifier systems and offline use, and resolution can still fail temporarily.

Defining another localization object here would duplicate `descriptions` and risk incompatible language-key rules.

## Meta-schema impact

Extend the object schema for `concepts` entries with optional `description` and `descriptions` members while continuing to reject other undeclared properties. The `descriptions` member should reference or reuse the corresponding map definition from the Alternate Names extension.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `concepts` entry may contain required `reference` and `kind`, optional `description`, and optional `descriptions`.
- `descriptions` follows JSON Structure Alternate Names and Descriptions Section 3.3, including its `lang:<BCP 47 tag>` keys.
- The specification defines the feature-enablement requirement for nested `descriptions`.
- Conformance text states that neither descriptive form affects semantic processing.
- The extension meta-schema accepts both optional members and rejects unrelated properties.
- An example demonstrates localized descriptions on multiple concept entries attached to one schema node.
